metadata.description: Pre-registered re-derivation of how closely Benford's law fits the leading digits of world country populations, on the 236-country x 74-year UN WPP panel (17,464 country-years, 8,732 per fold). Establishes that the intraclass correlation, not a ratio of mean squares, governs the frequency-type digit statistics; that the circular-mean statistic's degrees of freedom are the country count rather than any effective row count; and that a country-rotation randomization null supplies an exact cluster null whose kappa_i are the observed ones by construction.
metadata.method_name: country-rotation randomization null for Benford conformity on clustered panel data

examples.output: [even] The panel EXCEEDS its cluster envelope on the circular-mean statistic: |c1| = 0.07493 against a corrected two-sigma threshold of 0.05736 (5% threshold 0.07021; 80%-power MDA 0.08903), with observed within-country concentration mean kappa = 0.5421. All four frequency-type statistics are inside the same null, so the departure is specific to the BETWEEN-country phase alignment and not to the pooled digit histogram.
